newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka parliament approves new tax bill.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka parliament approves new tax bill.

text.p: Sri Lanka's parliament on Tuesday approved a new Goods and Services Tax (GST) bill, which will replace cumbersome turnover tax on imports, manufacturing and services.
"All developed countries use GST," Justice Minister and Deputy Finance Minister Gamini Lakshman Peiris told parliament. "It will make government tax collection more efficient."
Peiris said the anticipated higher tax revenue through GST will also help the government to cut its budget deficit to 7.5 percent of Gross Domestic Product this year.
The government managed to contain the deficit at 7.8 percent of GDP last year, the central bank said in its annual report last week. It was 8.3 percent in 1995.
The Central Bank said in the report large budget deficits have been the major macro-economic destabilising factor in Sri Lanka.
